thread:
Maya Chen: FYI customer reports embeddings endpoint returned 1536 dims instead of 768, and per-request latency jumped to ~700-1200ms. Only happens when they send batch_size=8. Dashboard sample rate dipped around 03:12 UTC. Request id: req_0a1b2c3
Devon Park: Can you paste the exact request payload and model param? Which route are they hitting — /v1/embeddings or our vectorize route?
Maya Chen: Hitting /v1/embeddings. Payload (sanitized): 
```json
{"model":"open-embed-v2-768","input":["sentence one","sentence two",...],"batch_size":8}
```
curl we gave them: 
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-v2-768","input":["a","b","c","d","e","f","g","h"]}'
```
Devon Park: thx. Any X-Trace or X-Request-ID in the response headers? Need a trace id to pull spans. Also ask them to enable `X-Debug-Traces: 1` header for a repro run.
Maya Chen: Found header: X-Trace: trace-7f9c. Dashboard link (internal): https://console.redwood/internal/dashboards/embeddings?since=03:00 (customer tenant masked).
ops-bot: trace-7f9c ingested -> route: embeddings-route-prod-3 -> model_variant: open-embed-v2-1536-compat (sampled) :gear:
Anika Shah: I saw a similar case yesterday. Runtime can route to a compat variant (1536) when batching + mixed seq lengths force a different kernel. That variant produces 1536-d embeddings to preserve alignment for quantized kernels.
Luis Ortega: If the fallback returns 1536 dims the customer's indexer will definitely fail. We need to ensure routing doesn't silently switch dims.
Devon Park: Repro checklist for eng-support: 1) exact curl/payload (done). 2) seq-length histogram of inputs (short vs long). 3) batch_size=8 reproduction run with X-Debug-Traces header. 4) indexer error logs from customer. Also share the trace id.
Maya Chen: I ran their repro with batch 8 locally: got dim:1536 and latency ~1s. Ran batch 4: dim 768 and latency ~220ms. Attaching short span from response: 
```
response: {"embedding":[...], "dim":1536, "request_id":"req_0a1b2c3"}
```
Anika Shah: Quick mitigation: reduce max_batch_size to 4 for that tenant or add routing rule to prefer the 768 variant. That will avoid the kernel path that triggers the compat fallback. If that works it's a stopgap.
Devon Park: I'll add a temporary routing rule to pin their traffic to open-embed-v2-768 for the next 24h while eng digs into kernel selection logic. ETA ~30m.
Luis Ortega: I'll open ST-4521 and add a dashboard panel for model_dim_mismatch.count and an alert when >0 in a minute window. Also annotate traces for easier hunting.
Maya Chen: One more data point — billing showed a token/compute spike during the window, looks like duplicate invocations in routing layer. Customer is on Dedicated. They want a fix asap.
ops-bot: Alert created: model_dim_mismatch: tenant=acct-54 severity=high -> incident INC-2026-331 created.
Devon Park: Action items: (Maya) collect full seq-length histogram + indexer error logs + full response headers for a failing request. (Anika/Luis) check kernel selection codepaths and add metric to runtime to prevent silent dim fallbacks. (Devon) deploy temporary routing pin and monitor.
Maya Chen: Will send customer the mitigation and ask them to run the reproduction with X-Debug-Traces. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
